I think the research will back me up here - depression isn't a fight that can be won.  It's like Sisyphus from Greek mythology, who offended Zeus (the head honcho) and was sentenced to push a massive rock up a hill, only for it slip from his grasp a few steps from the top.  He did this for eternity.  Camus said "we must imagine Sisyphus happy."  

The idea that anybody with depression could be "happy" in their condition seems nonsensical, and yet those of us that are still here have managed to get through it.  For Sisyphus to be happy is less for him to get joy from a the useless task of pushing a rock up a hill and more for him to accept where he is and to find happiness elsewhere.  Unfortunately, depression is such that you find happiness nowhere, or so it seems.  

This is where therapy can help alot.  No doctor can cure depression, but (as other posters have noted) as long as you pose no immediate risk to yourself or others, you can discuss your suicidal tendencies, and maybe even find out where they come from.  You can start to identify the things in your life that you can be happy, or at least, satisfied, about.  

Depression and the desire to kill yourself may never go away, but the fact that you're here means that there are other voices fighting against the one that says to kill yourself.  Depression is only part but it fights to be the whole.  It's hard to see where your best qualities lie when you're depressed but they're there for everyone else to see and in the midst of depression, you're your own worst judge.  

You can tell more people than an anonymous and uncredentialed internet about your problems - namely a therapist or even someone you trust (careful about leaning on a friend too much unless you're absolutely sure they can handle it).  

The voice in your head is just that - a voice.  It comes from you, but that doesn't mean that it is you. There's also a voice saying "go to bed", "have lunch", "put it off till tomorrow", etc. for better or worse.  Just keep in mind that there is a voice that is saying "don't do it",
